cuizhang: A wide garden rockery mountain made of stacked grey-white Taihu limestone (太湖石), many holes and grotesque shapes like ghosts and beasts, green moss patches and hanging vines, a narrow dark cave tunnel opening at the bottom center, about twice as wide as tall, Qing dynasty Chinese classical garden
linglong: A single tall vertical Taihu scholar's rock (太湖石峰), pale grey limestone, extremely perforated with many through-holes, slender twisted silhouette, standing on a small stone base, Chinese classical garden
paifang: A white marble Chinese memorial archway (玉石牌坊), four pillars and three openings, the center opening taller, carved coiling dragons on the pillars and beams, small carved stone hip roofs on top, Qing imperial style, white jade stone
shishi: A Qing dynasty Chinese guardian stone lion sitting on a rectangular carved pedestal, white marble, curly mane, one paw on an embroidered ball
fang: A small Chinese classical wooden pleasure boat (画舫) with a covered cabin with lattice windows and a curved tiled roof, reddish brown lacquered wood, flat bottom, about 6 meters long
bei: A Chinese stone stele (石碣) for an inscription: a rough-hewn upright grey stone slab with a smooth blank front face, set on a low stone base, rustic countryside style
ding: A large ancient Chinese bronze incense burner tripod (鼎) with two upright handles and three legs, dark green patina bronze, standing on a carved stone base
shizu: A small cluster of three Taihu garden rocks of different heights, pale grey perforated limestone, for decorating a Chinese courtyard
